access-log.userChipTitle: Click to remove this user filter

dashboard.glossarySub: {entries} entries · {failed} times a definition could not be applied

dashboard.knowledgeFound: found something for {used} of {searched} questions · {avg} pieces on average
dashboard.knowledgeUnused: not used in this period (off, or no questions)

dashboard.reportUnavailable: This report is not available to you.

data-access.checkTip: Reads one record id with your CRM rights (nothing is shown) to see whether the CRM lets the tool read this table
data-access.closedFieldsHint: Open this table to review and change its fields.
data-access.fieldsText: The primary id and name fields are locked open (the tool needs them to find records). Fields closed automatically have a sensitive-looking name.
data-access.intro: Choose which CRM tables and fields the chat tool may use. This is an extra protection on top of the CRM's own rights: a user can only ever see what the CRM allows AND what is open here. A closed table or field is never shown to the model and can not be used in any question (not as a column, filter, sort, grouping, total or count).
data-access.memoryOnly: These decisions are kept in the service's MEMORY only (the PostgreSQL connection is not configured). When the app pool restarts, every table or field you closed or opened is forgotten and the defaults apply again. Configure History:ConnectionString before relying on this list.
data-access.noDecision: No decision has been made yet: only the starting list is open and every other table is closed. Open the tables your users need (for example custom tables), review the automatically closed fields, and keep sensitive tables closed.
data-access.notAvailable: The data access list is not available to you.
data-access.note: This list applies to the chat tool only. In a CRM view opened with "Open in CRM" a closed field does not appear as a column, but a user can add that column in the CRM view themselves; what applies inside the CRM is the CRM's own field security. Set that up as well for customers with sensitive data.
data-access.openItTip: The field becomes usable in the chat tool
data-access.pickTable: Pick a table on the left to see its status and fields.
data-access.resetTip: Remove your decision: the default applies again
data-access.reviewText: These field names look sensitive (national id, IBAN, salary, credit, birth date...). They are closed until you decide. The name rule is only a hint: a sensitive field with an ordinary name is NOT detected, so review the other fields of customers with sensitive data too.
data-access.reviewTitle: {n} fields were closed automatically — please review
data-access.reviewTitleOne: 1 field was closed automatically — please review
data-access.switchedOff: The data access list is switched OFF (setting Access:DataPolicy = off). Nothing is filtered right now. Switch it on again in Settings > Access.
data-access.title: Data access
data-access.toggleCloseTip: The tool stops using this table
data-access.toggleOpenTip: First checks that the CRM lets the tool read this table
design.intro: Describe a business requirement and the assistant drafts a customization design: whether an existing table already covers it, the tables, fields and relationships to add, views, security notes and open questions. It reads the CRM schema (table and field names only, never records) and creates nothing in the CRM. What you type is sent to the language model. A design can take a few minutes; it keeps running if you leave this page.
design.notAvailableToYou: The design assistant is not available to you.
design.problemsNote: The built-in check found {n} point(s) the design should be reviewed for; they are listed at the end of the document.
design.requirementPlaceholder: For example: We want to track dealer service appointments. Each appointment has a vehicle, a customer, a date, a status (planned, completed, cancelled) and a list of operations done. One appointment can have several operations.
design.started: Started. This can take a few minutes; you can leave this page and come back.
design.title: Design assistant
design.unavailable: This design is no longer available.
documents.emptyText: Add the first one: a business term, a field explanation or a rule.
documents.intro: Company knowledge the model reads when it answers a question: what a business term means, which field to use, which old field to avoid. Turkish, English or mixed text all work.
documents.modelDoesNotRead: The model does not read documents yet (Knowledge:Enabled is off). You can already add documents and try questions below.
documents.modelReads: The model reads these documents when it answers questions.
documents.noPersonalData: Do not write personal data (names, IDs, phone numbers, customer records) here. Documents are read by the model and shared company-wide. Longer than a few paragraphs? Split it into several documents.
documents.notAvailable: Documents are not available to you.
documents.nothingFound: Nothing relevant found: the model would get no company knowledge for this question.
documents.saving: Saving… (the text is turned into search vectors on this machine)
documents.switchedOff: The knowledge base is switched off: {reason}. Everything else works. Install the pgvector extension in PostgreSQL and restart the service to turn it on.
documents.templateHint:
Tip: write one idea per paragraph, e.g.
Term: Active customer
Definition: an account of type Customer with an order in the last 12 months.
CRM: account, customertypecode
Example question: show our active customers
documents.title: Documents
documents.tryIntro: Type a question as an analyst would. You see which document pieces the model would read for it, best first. Use this to check a new document is found.
documents.turnedOff: Document turned off: the model no longer sees it.
export.about_accesslog: Who read which CRM tables, when, and how many rows. It never holds question text, filter values or the data itself.
export.about_audit: Who changed what in this tool: users, roles, settings, refused attempts and every earlier export.
export.about_feedback: Per day: answers rated helpful or not. Totals only; no question text, no person.
export.about_questions: WHAT users asked, with the user and the time. Only questions asked while question-text viewing was on, and only until the user deletes the chat or it expires. Handle the file like personal data.
export.about_usage: Per day: questions asked, failed ones, model calls and tokens. Totals only; no person is named.
export.intro: Download logs as a file for audits, investigations or your own security monitoring. Every export is written to the audit trail: who, when, which data and range, and a SHA-256 of the file. Question text is never included.
export.notAvailable: Export is not available to you.
export.noViewPerm: You may export, but you have no view permission for any data set. Ask an administrator.
export.started:
Download started: {file}.
The audit trail now shows export.start. When the file is complete it adds export.done with the row count, the size and the SHA-256 of what was sent.
export.title: Export
export.verifyP1: Open the Audit trail and find the export.done entry for your file (it names the data set and holds rows, bytes and sha256). Then compute the hash of the downloaded file and compare:
export.verifyP2: The hash covers exactly the bytes the server sent (CSV files start with a UTF-8 byte order mark). If the file was cut short, the entry says export.aborted or export.failed and its hash is marked partial. Times are written both in UTC and in the time zone shown in the time_zone column.
exportcol.accesslog.outcome: ok, crm_denied (the CRM refused) or error.
exportcol.accesslog.request_id: Groups the reads that belong to the same question.
exportcol.accesslog.source: Where the read came from: ask, result, lookup, record_context, count, summary, draft or other.
exportcol.accesslog.tables: CRM tables that were read, separated by semicolons. Table names only.
exportcol.accesslog.user_id: CRM system user id of the person whose data access this was.
exportcol.accesslog.user_name: Name of that user as the CRM knows it (empty when it could not be resolved).
exportcol.audit.action: What was done, for example user.add, role.update, access.denied, export.done.
exportcol.audit.actor: Account that did it (or 'bootstrap' for the configured first administrator).
exportcol.audit.detail: Short description of the change. Never contains question text or CRM record contents.
exportcol.audit.target: What it was done to: an account, a role, a group, a table or an endpoint.
exportcol.common.time_local: The same moment in the time zone named in time_zone, ISO 8601 with its UTC offset.
exportcol.common.time_utc: When it happened, ISO 8601 in UTC (ends with Z).
exportcol.common.time_zone: The IANA time zone used for time_local (the browser's zone, or the server's when none was given).
exportcol.feedback.thumbs_down: Answers rated not helpful that day.
exportcol.questions.question: The question as typed. Only questions asked while the Access:QuestionTextView setting was on are included; they disappear when the user deletes the chat or it expires.
exportcol.questions.table: The main CRM table the question was about.
exportcol.questions.user_id: CRM system user id of the person who asked.
exportcol.questions.user_name: Name of that user as the CRM knows it (empty when it could not be resolved).
feedback.copyTitle: Copy the question and its explanation
feedback.intro: Questions people chose to share when they rated an answer thumbs down. They stay in your system: nothing is sent anywhere automatically. If you want to share an example with the developers, copy it yourself. Each time you open this page it is written to the audit trail.
feedback.notAvailable: This page is not available to you.
feedback.noteDays: Shared questions are kept for up to {days} days, or until the user withdraws them or the chat is deleted (by the user, or by the chat history retention).
feedback.noteForever: Shared questions are kept until the user withdraws them or the chat is deleted (by the user, or by the chat history retention).
feedback.title: Feedback
glossary.brokenWarn: {n} entries are broken (their table or field is closed or gone). They are ignored until fixed.
glossary.descHelp: A short plain sentence, for example: Accounts with more than 1000 employees.
glossary.docConflict: Note: these knowledge documents also mention the term: {docs}. Make sure they say the same thing.
glossary.empty: No entries yet. Add your first term.
glossary.fDescription: Note (shown to the model and in the answer's explanation)
glossary.fKindAliasHelp: An alias tells the model which table (and field) a word means. It is a hint and is not enforced.
glossary.fKindFilterHelp: A filter stands for conditions. Whenever the question uses the term, the query must contain exactly these conditions, or the question is not answered.
glossary.fTermsHelp: Every way people say it, in any language. Endings are understood (for example kobi, kobiler, kobi'nin).
glossary.importHelp: Choose a glossary JSON file (from Export). It is checked first; nothing is added until you confirm.
glossary.loadError: The glossary could not be loaded.
glossary.notPersistent: The glossary is kept in memory only: entries are lost when the service restarts. Connect the PostgreSQL history database to keep them.
glossary.reason_attribute_unavailable: That field is not available (it may be closed in Data access).
glossary.reason_conditions_missing: Add at least one condition (6 at most).
glossary.reason_duplicate: One of these terms already belongs to another entry.
glossary.reason_entity_unavailable: Choose a table the tool is allowed to use.
glossary.reason_invalid_json: The file is not a glossary export.
glossary.reason_limit: The glossary is full. Raise Glossary:MaxEntries in Settings or delete entries.
glossary.reason_operator_not_allowed: That condition is not possible for this kind of field.
glossary.reason_option_unknown: That option does not exist on the field.
glossary.reason_terms_invalid: Add 1 to 6 terms of 2 to 60 characters each.
glossary.reason_type_unsupported: This kind of field cannot be used in a glossary.
glossary.reason_value_invalid: A value does not fit the field.
glossary.reason_value_missing: Enter a value for every condition.
glossary.relationalNote: Terms that need counting or related records (for example "loyal customer = 3 or more orders in the last 12 months") cannot be defined here yet. Write them as plain text on the Documents page instead.
glossary.sub: Teach the tool your company's words. A term can point to a table (an alias) or stand for conditions (a filter, for example: large company = more than 1000 employees). Filters are checked by code in every query.
glossary.switchedOff: The glossary is switched off (Settings, Features). Entries are kept but not used.
glossary.title: Business glossary
glossary.tryAlias: An alias runs nothing. It points to: {text}
glossary.tryError: The count could not be completed.
glossary.tryNote: Counted with your own CRM rights. The records themselves are not shown.
glossary.tryNotReadable: You are not allowed to read this table in the CRM, so it could not be counted.
groups.intro: Give everyone in a Windows (AD) group the same roles. Members get in without being added one by one. You can only give roles whose permissions you have yourself.
groups.noGroupsFound: No groups found in your sign-in (type the name)
groups.notAvailable: AD groups are not available to you.
groups.pickLabel: Pick one of my AD groups
groups.roleLocked: This role holds permissions you do not have yourself, so you cannot give or take it away.

identity.mappedGroups: Mapped AD groups you belong to

identity.modeOn: on: only users who hold the App.Use permission may use the tool.
identity.modeReport: report: nobody is blocked, but users who would be blocked are written to the audit trail with their AD groups.
identity.noGroups: none (the identity mode may not carry groups, or they could not be read)

logs.intro: Warnings and errors from the service. Never contains question text or CRM rows. Click a row to see the full details.
logs.notAvailable: Logs are not available to you.
logs.showingLatest: Showing the latest {count}. Narrow the filters to see older ones.
logs.title: Application logs
perm.AccessLog.View: View the data access log: who read which CRM tables and how many rows (no question text)
perm.DataPolicy.Manage: Choose which CRM tables and fields the chat tool may use (on top of the CRM rights); every change is written to the audit trail
perm.Design.Use: Use the customization design assistant: it reads the CRM schema (table and field names only, never records) and writes a design proposal as a document. It creates nothing in the CRM. Requirements you type are sent to the language model
perm.Documents.Manage: Add, edit and remove the company knowledge documents the model reads
perm.Export.Run: Download logs as a file (CSV or JSON Lines): the audit trail, the data access log, usage and feedback counts. Needs the matching view permission too; every export is written to the audit trail with a SHA-256 of the file
perm.Feedback.View: Read the questions users chose to share to improve the tool (golden set candidates; no user names, no result rows); every view is audited
perm.Glossary.Manage: Define the company terms the chat tool understands (for example: large company means more than 1000 employees): add, test, import and export them. Definitions hold rules, never record data; every change is audited
perm.Metadata.Refresh: Refresh the CRM metadata cache (after entities or fields changed)
perm.Quality.Manage: Build and run the acceptance set: generate cases from the schema, approve or retire them, export them. Cases hold questions and reference queries, never result rows; every change is audited
perm.Questions.View: Read what users asked (question text). Works only while the Access:QuestionTextView setting is on; every view is audited
perm.Roles.Manage: Edit what each role may do
perm.Settings.Manage: Change runtime settings: question limits, pause asking, knowledge base and retention
quality.counts: Passed {passed} · Failed {failed} · Sometimes failed {flaky} · Errors {errors} · Skipped {skipped} · Not readable {unreadable} · Unverified {unverified}
quality.dataChangedNote: {n} case(s) have different reference data than in the previous run. Both sides were compared on today's data, so a changed result is still a real result.
quality.exportHelp: Downloads the active cases in the evaluation format (run with --cases from the command line).
quality.finished_cancelled: The check was cancelled; the results so far are kept.
quality.firstRunNote: This is the first finished run, so there is nothing to compare with yet.
quality.generateHelp: Reads each chosen table with your own CRM rights and creates up to seven cases per table (count, list, filter, chart, highest, lowest, per lookup). Generated cases start unverified and are not counted until you approve them. Closed tables and sensitive fields are never used.
quality.intro: The acceptance set: questions with a verified reference query. Cases hold the question and the query, never result rows. Generate cases from your CRM schema, read them, approve the ones that are right, and export the set to check the tool again after an update.
quality.latency: Time per case: average {avg} s, 95th percentile {p95} s, slowest {max} s
quality.noAccuracy: No verified cases were checked, so there is no accuracy yet.
quality.none: No cases yet. Generate some from the schema above.
quality.noRegressions: Nothing that passed in the previous run fails now.
quality.notAvailable: The quality check is switched off (setting Features:Quality) or you do not have permission.
quality.nothingSelected: Select at least one case first.
quality.notPersistent: The acceptance set is kept in memory only: it is lost when the app restarts. Configure the history database to keep it.
quality.reason_unknown_or_closed: the table is unknown or closed
quality.repeatHelp: Asking the same case several times shows cases that sometimes pass and sometimes fail.
quality.runHelp: Asks every active case to the tool as a user would, runs your reference query next to it with your own CRM rights, and compares the two results. It runs in the background (a local model can take hours); you can leave this page, cancel, or come back later. Closed data is skipped; no result rows are stored.
quality.skippedNote: Skipped cases use data that is closed or no longer available; they are not model mistakes.
quality.title: Quality check
quality.unreadableNote: Not readable: your CRM rights do not allow reading that data; they are not model mistakes.
quality.unverifiedNote: Unverified cases ran but are not counted in the accuracy. Approve the ones that are right.
question-view.countRecorded: Questions: {n} (this view was recorded in the audit trail)
question-view.intro: Read what one user asked. This is switched off by default (Settings > Access: Access:QuestionTextView). While it is on, users see a notice in the chat window, only questions asked while it was on can be read, and every time you look it is written to the audit trail (who, whose, how many; never the text).
question-view.notAvailable: Not available: the feature is switched off (Settings > Access: Access:QuestionTextView = on turns it on), or you do not have the permission.
question-view.nothing: Nothing to show: either no question was asked while the setting was on, or the user deleted them.
question-view.title: Question texts
question-view.typeAccount: Type a Windows account (DOMAIN\user) or a CRM user id.
roles.builtInNote: Built in. Always has every permission, including future ones. It cannot be edited or deleted.
roles.cannotGive: You do not have this permission yourself, so you cannot give it.
roles.intro: A role is a set of permissions. You can only give a permission that you have yourself.
roles.notAvailable: Roles are not available to you.
roles.roleDeleted: Role deleted. Users who had it lost its permissions.
roles.title: Roles
setting.Access:DataPolicy: The data access list (which CRM tables and fields the chat tool may use, set in Data access). on = closed tables and fields are never shown to the model or used in any query (default). off = EMERGENCY ONLY: nothing is filtered; every change of this switch is written to the audit trail.
setting.Access:QuestionTextView: Let administrators with the Questions.View permission read what users asked (the question text). off = nobody can (default). on = only questions asked while this is on can be read, users see a notice in the chat window, and every view is written to the audit trail. Users deleting a chat also removes it here.
setting.Access:RequireAppUse: Who may use the chat tool. off = everyone the CRM knows (today's behaviour); report = nobody is blocked, but users who would be blocked are written to the audit log with their AD groups; on = only users who hold the App.Use permission (the admin panel is never affected).
setting.Conversation:ContextMinutes: How long after an answer a follow-up question may build on it, in minutes (older answers are treated as a fresh start)
setting.Counting:TimeoutSeconds: Longest time the "how many records in total" count of a truncated result may take, in seconds (the result is shown immediately; the number is filled in when it arrives)
setting.Design:TimeoutMinutes: Longest one customization design may run, in minutes. It runs in the background; a design that takes longer is stopped and marked failed.
setting.Export:MaxRows: Most rows one log export file may contain. A larger range stops at this many rows (the audit trail says so); narrow the date range or filters to get the rest.
setting.Features:EmailDraft: Write email drafts for a customer or contact (for example: write a follow-up email to this customer). The model writes a template with placeholders; the values (names, counts, dates) are filled in by code from queries run as the user, and no record data goes to the model. Drafts are text only: nothing is sent and nothing is written to the CRM.
setting.Features:Feedback: Let users rate answers with thumbs up / down and a reason. Only the rating, the reason and technical details (tables, steps, time) are kept; no question text.
setting.Features:Glossary: Business glossary: company terms that administrators define (for example: big company means more than 1000 employees) are applied to matching questions, and the query is checked by code to include them. No record data is involved.
setting.Features:OpenInCrm: Let users open a large (truncated) result in the CRM's own list view (paging and Excel export are handled by the CRM). WRITES one personal view per user into the CRM (named "NL Query - last result") on that user's behalf. Off by default. Before turning it on: give the service account the personal view rights (Setup-ServiceAccount-Crm.ps1 -OpenInCrm) and give the Records.OpenInCrm permission to the roles that may use it.
setting.Features:Quality: Quality check in the admin panel: build an acceptance set (cases generated from the CRM schema or saved from real answers) and check that the tool still answers them correctly. Cases hold questions and reference queries, never result rows.
setting.Features:ShowFetchXml: Show the raw FetchXML under every answer (for administrators and developers). Off by default: users see a plain-language explanation of the query instead.
setting.Features:Summary: Answer "summarize this customer" with a fixed customer summary (basic details, open opportunities, recent activities, open cases, contracts, orders, other related tables). Built by code from queries run as the user; no model reads any record.
setting.Feedback:AllowSharing: Let a user who rates an answer thumbs down choose to share the question text and its explanation with administrators (golden set candidates). Never on by default for the user; off here hides the choice.
setting.Glossary:MaxEntries: Most entries the business glossary may hold.
setting.History:RetentionDays: Days to keep chat history (pinned chats are kept); users see this number in the chat window; 0 = keep forever
setting.Knowledge:Enabled: Let the model read the company knowledge documents when it answers
setting.Knowledge:MaxChars: Most characters of document text added to one question
setting.Knowledge:MinSimilarity: How close a document piece must be to the question to be used (0 to 1; higher = stricter)
setting.Knowledge:TopK: Most document pieces added to one question
setting.Limits:AskDeadlineSeconds: Longest time one question may take, in seconds
setting.Limits:AskEnabled: Allow users to ask questions. Turn off to pause asking (emergency stop).
setting.Limits:CloudDailyTokenBudget: Daily token budget for the cloud model (lab only); 0 = unlimited
setting.Limits:MaxConcurrentPerUser: Questions one user may have running at the same time
setting.Limits:MaxConcurrentTotal: Questions running at the same time across all users (protects the model server)
setting.Limits:MaxConditions: Most conditions one generated query may have
setting.Limits:MaxLinkDepth: Deepest nesting of joins in one generated query
setting.Limits:MaxLinkEntities: Most joins (link-entity) one generated query may have
setting.Limits:MaxRecordNameChars: Longest record name sent to the model, in characters
setting.Limits:QuestionsPerDay: Questions one user may ask per day (UTC)
setting.Limits:QuestionsPerMinute: Questions one user may ask in any 60 seconds
setting.Metadata:CacheMinutes: How long the CRM table and field list is kept before it is read again, in minutes. New tables and fields reach the chat within this time (the Refresh CRM metadata button does it at once).
setting.Metrics:RetentionDays: Days to keep usage metrics and application logs; 0 = keep forever
setting.Planning:CacheMinutes: How long a verified query plan is reused for the identical question, in minutes (0 = off)
setting.Quality:MaxCases: Most cases the acceptance set may hold. Generating stops when the limit is reached.
setting.Quality:RunTimeoutMinutes: Longest one quality check run may take, in minutes. It runs in the background; a run that takes longer is stopped and marked failed.
setting.Retention:DesignDays: Days to keep finished customization designs (the requirement text and the result; only their owner can see them); 0 = keep forever.
setting.Retention:FeedbackDays: Days to keep the questions users chose to share (golden set candidates); 0 = keep forever. A shared question also goes away when the user deletes the chat or withdraws it, and when the chat itself is removed by History:RetentionDays (pinned chats are kept).
setting.Retention:QualityRunDays: Days to keep finished quality check runs and their per-case results (questions and verdicts, never result rows); 0 = keep forever.
setting.Retention:SecurityLogDays: Days to keep the data access log (who read which CRM tables, how many rows; no question text); 0 = keep forever. The admin audit trail is never deleted.
setting.Summary:SectionTimeoutSeconds: Longest time one section of a customer summary may take, in seconds (a slow section shows as unavailable; the others still appear)
setting.Ui:DefaultLanguage: Language of the chat window, result page and admin panel for users who have not chosen one and whose browser language is not supported. Users can change their own language from the chat window's settings menu. en = English, tr = Turkish.
settings.askOnText: Users can ask questions. Pause asking to stop all new questions for everyone within seconds (an emergency stop). Questions already running finish; this admin panel keeps working.
settings.askPausedText: New questions are refused with a clear message (HTTP 503). This admin panel keeps working. Resume asking when the problem is solved.
settings.groupDescAccess: Who may use the tool and what the administrators may see.
settings.groupDescCapacity: Limits that protect the server: how many questions, how long they may run, how big exports may be.
settings.groupDescContent: Time limits for counting records and building customer summaries.
settings.groupDescConversation: How a follow-up question is tied to the previous answer.
settings.groupDescFeatures: Switch features on or off. A switch saves as soon as you click it.
settings.groupDescInterface: Language and other things users see.
settings.groupDescKnowledge: The company knowledge documents the tool may use when it understands a question.
settings.groupDescPlanning: How long the tool remembers query plans and the CRM schema.
settings.groupDescRetention: How many days records are kept before they are deleted. 0 means keep them forever.
settings.notAvailable: Settings are not available to you.
settings.pauseConfirm: Click again to pause for everyone
settings.pickGroup: Pick a group on the left.
settings.resetTitle: Go back to the settings file value or the default
settings.sub: Limits and switches the service reads while it runs. A change applies at once on this server (other servers pick it up within 30 seconds) and is written to the audit trail. Keys, passwords, sign-in and connection settings can only be changed in the settings file.
settings.title: Settings
